items.title: Google open-sources AQuA, an ambient agent that diagnoses your production agent's failures
items.summary: AQuA runs beside a deployed agent, outside its request path, and samples recent sessions from Cloud Trace, Logging, or BigQuery. It reviews each against a checklist, clusters shared failure mechanisms, verifies clusters against full transcripts before surfacing them, and tracks them as new, recurring, or resolved. Released as composable building blocks in google/adk-recipes; a local demo needs no cloud project. On the authors' own 32-session replay, full-session passes went from 5/32 to 13/32 after a one-line prompt fix the tool surfaced.
items.why: This is the missing piece between an agent demo working and an agent running in production: a way to see what it is actually failing on, verified against real transcripts rather than a made-up confidence score.
items.action: Clone google/adk-recipes and run the included local demo on synthetic data before pointing it at anything real.

items.title: Anthropic ships OSS Scanner -- free AI security scans for open-source projects, sent with zero human review
items.summary: Part of Anthropic's new Cyber Mission: enrolled open-source projects get periodic scans from Anthropic's strongest models, with reports including a proof of concept, an explanation, and a suggested fix where one exists. Reports are model-generated and sent without human review; Anthropic expects a true-positive rate above 90% at launch.
items.why: A security report that reaches you with no human ever having read it first is a real trust test for AI-generated findings -- worth seeing what it flags on code you actually know well.
items.action: If you maintain an open-source repo, enroll and see what its first scan cycle flags against issues you already know about.
